name: skeleton
description: A grey placeholder in the shape of what is loading (a table row, a sidebar item, a block, a paper sheet). Shown while a container waits for its data, removed when the content renders.

props.name: variant
props.description: "row" (small square plus bars), "item" (one bar, sidebar), "block" (two lines, CV block) or "page" (a landscape sheet, preview panes).

rationale: Pages used to show empty containers (or false empty states) until their API calls returned. A skeleton shows the shape of what is coming: bars at the width of typical cells, in bg.surface-pressed, pulsing in opacity (1.4s, still under prefers-reduced-motion). It is declarative: data-skeleton="row:4" on a container, filled by component.js when the HTML is parsed, cleared as soon as real content is added to the container (or with dsSkeleton.clear()); a 10s fail-safe clears it anyway. grid-column: 1 / -1 makes one placeholder span all columns of a grid table. [data-skeleton-hide] hides an empty state meanwhile. Not sourced from Figma (explicit request 2026-10-12). Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: Placeholders are aria-hidden; the container carries aria-busy="true" while they are shown. The pulse is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
